races.name: Newgrange Hotel Handicap

runners_data.name: Thurso
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front-runner; won over this course and trip on Firm last time out suggesting the good-to-firm is ideal, but apprentice Sam Coen carries a small fitness question after 34 days off and the STYLE_FIT flag reflects a horse capable of more when given a genuine lead rather than a scrappy pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Thurso landed a win two starts back and backed it up with a battling 4th last time, 34 days ago, with today's trip and ground both already proven. Second of 16 on our figures from draw 11, he just needs to rediscover that winning zip.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Pairc
runners_data.note: W J Lee takes the mount for a yard in form (T14: 1/17); genuine hold-up horse who stays all day but has been running over 7f-8f — dropping to 6f on good-to-firm is a potential trip concern given zero wins at this distance in the last five runs.
runners_data.comment: Phoenix Pairc won four starts back but has lost the thread since, following with a 9th and two blank efforts, the latest 23 days ago. She has raced over today's trip and rates 70, fifth of 16 from draw 12 — capable but out of sorts.

runners_data.name: Poweracclaim
runners_data.note: Ben Coen is a serious booking for J P Murtagh, who has been busy lately (T14: 2/22); has finished third or fourth repeatedly and the 6f good-going profile fits — the question is whether he can convert near-miss form when sitting prominently off a slow pace.
runners_data.comment: Poweracclaim sits highest of 16 on our figures, staying competitive in four of his last five starts and never worse than 5th bar one blank effort. He has already raced over today's trip; a 38-day absence is the main knock on his claims.

runners_data.name: In The Gloaming
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old for Adrian Oliver who has only been seen three times; genuine hold-up style suits a scenario where the pace quickens, but limited form in the book and just 3 runs on similar going makes this a significant unknown.
runners_data.comment: In The Gloaming has settled into a pair of 5ths after a blank effort before that, his latest run 27 days ago. He has raced over today's trip and rates 67, seventh of 16 — steady but still without a win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Aurora Nova
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with genuine form credentials on good ground (2 wins, 4 places in 15 similar-going runs); Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim is useful, and she has been running respectably at shorter trips — a hold-up runner who needs the pace to genuinely lift.
runners_data.comment: Aurora Nova was a solid 3rd three starts back but has faded to 5th and 9th since, the latest just 34 days ago. She has raced over today's trip and going, and a strong speed figure of 76 hints at more ability than her rating of 67 shows.

runners_data.name: Are You In Or Out
runners_data.note: Back quickly after just 10 days, which for a five-year-old in form (1 win 6f good ground) reads as a confident trainer move; prominent style suits this race perfectly and Nicola Burns's 5lb claim eases the weight burden considerably.
runners_data.comment: Are You In Or Out won three starts back but has since slipped to 7th and an unplaced effort just 10 days ago. She has raced over today's trip and going, and that quick turnaround keeps her sharp; rated 67, ninth of 16.

runners_data.name: Gotta Catch'em All
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent but mapped to midfield because the field is overloaded with P-style runners; recent form over 8f-10f distances looks too long for a 6f dash, headgear (blinkers) may sharpen focus, but the STYLE_FIT discount and trip queries combine as negatives.
runners_data.comment: Gotta Catch'em All is a model of consistency, finishing between 4th and 9th in each of his last five, latest just 8 days ago. He has raced over today's trip and going, and a big speed figure of 76 outstrips his rating of 67.

runners_data.name: Irish Rumour
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes this, which immediately elevates interest; form shows two second-place finishes over 6f-7f on good ground and a prominent style that fits the likely race shape — the top jockey booking is the standout positive angle here.
runners_data.comment: Irish Rumour has twice been runner-up in her last five starts but has blank efforts either side, including her latest, 23 days ago. She has raced over today's trip and rates 64, 11th of 16 — she has the placed form but needs more consistency.

runners_data.name: Coincidental Glory
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness yard has been punching (T14: 3/27) and Declan McDonogh is a consistent booking; three-year-old who has placed four times without winning suggests a horse that finds one too good — prominent style fits but the pattern of finding nil off a slow pace is a worry.
runners_data.comment: Coincidental Glory shook off a below-par spell to finish a solid 3rd last time, 22 days ago. He has raced over today's trip, carries a strong speed figure of 75, and sits third of 16 on our figures — his official mark lags behind that level.

runners_data.name: Reinforce
runners_data.note: True hold-up runner who needs others to set a genuine pace; has been finishing midfield to rear over 5f, and the step up to 6f on a tight Navan track could help, but 17 days since last run for a yard with no recent runners (T14: 0/0) limits confidence.
runners_data.comment: Reinforce has struggled to make an impact, another below-par effort at the tail of the field coming 17 days ago. He does have both today's trip and ground covered, and a big speed figure of 74 offers hope from a rating of 62, 13th of 16.

runners_data.name: Elly Bay
runners_data.note: Three-year-old returning after just 10 days, carrying top apprentice James Ryan; naturally prominent, has placed over 6f-7f on good ground before, but finishing position 9 most recently over 6f on a similar surface is hard to overcome.
runners_data.comment: Elly Bay built nicely to finish runner-up two starts back, but could not back it up when only 9th last time, just 10 days ago. She has raced over today's trip and sits fourth of 16 on our figures — questionable whether that flat run was a blip.

runners_data.name: Verified
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a finish-fade flag and a recent form line of 9-0002 — the two near the frame came on Soft or Heavy ground, and the good-to-firm here looks likely to expose that preference; Leigh Roche is reliable but this profile does not suit today's anticipated shape.
runners_data.comment: Verified turned in his best effort for a while with a clear 2nd last time, 22 days ago, having found only rear-of-field finishes before that. He has raced over today's trip, and a big speed figure of 74, well clear of his rating of 67, hints at more to come.

runners_data.name: Prime Sign
runners_data.note: True hold-up type redistributed into midfield due to field depth; the finish-fade flag is damaging over just 6f on a quick surface, and a form line of 605-00 with one win in 9 similar-going attempts gives very little reason to be optimistic regardless of pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Prime Sign has managed only a modest 5th and 6th among mostly blank efforts, the latest 29 days ago. She has raced over today's trip and rates 63, 12th of 16 — hard to fancy, though a useful speed figure of 72 offers a sliver of encouragement.

runners_data.name: The Cosy Corner
runners_data.note: Two-year-old form only in the book; 317 days off is a massive fitness query and all three career runs have been in defeat — Chris Hayes is capable but this horse is essentially an unknown quantity returning from a long absence on the quickest ground it has faced.
runners_data.comment: The Cosy Corner is bottom of the pile on our figures, rated 48. Her last run, a 9th, came all of 317 days ago, with two blank efforts before that in her recent record, though she does have today's trip covered.

runners_data.name: Dubai Opulence
runners_data.note: Three-year-old returning for Miss Lupini with minimal form to recommend it: 0 wins and 0 places in four career starts, all on going described as good or easier, and Killian Leonard faces a stiff task to do anything with this profile in a 16-runner competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: Dubai Opulence has continued to toil, following a pair of rear-of-field finishes with two more blank efforts, the latest 29 days ago. He has raced over today's trip previously, but a rating of 50, 15th of 16, leaves him hard to fancy on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Step Back In Time
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran with a natural prominent style but redistributed because there is simply no room for another P-type to get to the front; form shows 13th-9th-14th-12th in recent 6f good-ground runs, and the STYLE_FIT discount reflects genuine role conflict.
runners_data.comment: Step Back In Time has struggled recently, three blanks and a 9th since a modest 7th, her latest run just 10 days ago. She has raced over today's trip and going, and a rating of 60 sits well above her official mark of 44 despite that form.

races.paceDynamic: Thurso is the only confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner field and, with no genuine challenger pressing for the lead, is set to dictate from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Navan. That controlled pace is likely to compress the field through the middle stages, keeping the race together longer than a truly contested sprint would — conditions that suit horses who can sit close to the pace and produce a sharp finish rather than those who need a genuine end-to-end test to close. The redistribution of Gotta Catch'em All and Step Back In Time — both natural prominent types who are unlikely to secure their preferred position in a field already stacked with P-style runners — will cause friction in the early stages and may force some jockeys to be patient when they would rather be forward. With the pace comfortable and the good-to-firm ground placing a premium on fluency and a quick turn of foot in the final two furlongs, this race shape most clearly favours horses able to race prominently or in the first quarter of the field and produce a clean acceleration — confirmed Prominent types like Poweracclaim, Irish Rumour, Coincidental Glory, and Are You In Or Out are best placed to exploit Thurso's uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Thurso dictates an unhurried gallop and prominent-tracking horses get a clean run from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Thurso sets a steady tempo that bunches the field, allowing those sitting just behind to strike without burning energy in a battle for position; the good-to-firm surface rewards quick acceleration from P-style horses who are always travelling.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent brigade get into a tighter scrimmage than expected and the pace quickens enough to open ground for midfield horses in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A slightly busier pace than forecast creates enough stringing-out for horses running from the middle to pick up dropped rivals; Aurora Nova and In The Gloaming, genuine hold-up types with good-to-firm form, would be the main beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Leader Doubles Up
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so conservative that Thurso simply idles clear and the field never truly gets organised to chase.
scenarios.body: With no pressure on Thurso at any stage, the race degenerates into a sprint from too far out for the closers to bridge the gap; horses who can latch on immediately behind the leader and strike alongside Thurso in the final furlong are the threat.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrimmage Suits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of Gotta Catch'em All and Step Back In Time causes early crowding and the race becomes unexpectedly messy and fast-paced.
scenarios.body: A chaotic early tempo would spread the field and, unusually, open a slipstream for a fresh-legged hold-up runner arriving late; given the field size and tight weights this is a low-probability outcome but Phoenix Pairc or Reinforce could sneak a place.

watchPoints.text: Watch how quickly Gotta Catch'em All and Step Back In Time try to push forward at the break — if both go for the same ground in the first furlong, the early scrimmage could accelerate the pace beyond what Thurso's connections intend and alter the entire race shape.

Irish Rumour with Dylan Browne McMonagle is the jockey booking that could shift the market; if McMonagle sends him forward early rather than sitting prominent, this horse could be harder to catch than the odds suggest.

Thurso's price and race viability hinge entirely on Sam Coen (apprentice, 5lb) controlling the fractions — if the pace is misjudged too fast, the leader runs herself into the ground before the two-furlong mark and the entire scenario collapses.

The good-to-firm surface is confirmed across all races on the card, meaning the draw and early positioning become even more critical at Navan's tight track — horses getting shuffled back in a 16-runner field over 6f face a difficult task on a surface that does not encourage dramatic late finishes.

Monitor the weight of market support for Are You In Or Out — returning after just 10 days with a 5lb claimer on board and proven 6f good-ground form; if connections are confident enough to run so quickly, it may represent a live angle that the pace map underscores.

races.name: Navan Adventure Centre Handicap

runners_data.name: All Hail
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed pace-setter who has shown the ability to dominate over 6f on good ground; the drop to 5f is interesting but a fade flag and four recent misses temper enthusiasm, even if uncontested lead suits tactically.
runners_data.comment: All Hail claimed a battling 2nd two starts back, and although that form dipped again with an 8th last time, he carries 140 lb and rates a fair 74, fourth of 10. He has already raced over today's trip, but a 44-day absence is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: The Right One
runners_data.note: Won last time over this exact 5f on soft, and has solid placed form over the trip on good — the return to quicker ground is the key question, but seven runs at similar going with four placed efforts suggest they handle it adequately; prominent style fits this race shape well.
runners_data.comment: The Right One won last time out, 22 days ago, backing up a 2nd and 3rd earlier in the campaign, with just one blip two starts back. She has raced over today's trip and going, and a rating of 76, third of 10, makes her a leading threat here.

runners_data.name: White Smoke
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer dropping back to 5f after mixed form; apprentice claim of 7lb is the headline angle, but their natural rear-of-field style is disadvantaged in a race where the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to bring them into play.
runners_data.comment: White Smoke ran to a fair 4th last time, just 8 days ago, despite a stop-start campaign that included a 9th. She has raced over today's trip, and a strong speed figure of 71 explains why she rates second of 10 despite ordinary recent finishes.

runners_data.name: Amerilis
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a tongue tie fitted, showing a second at 6f on good ground as their best recent effort; drops in trip but the prominent style fits the race shape, and Donagh O'Connor is an able jockey for a horse that needs to be on the bridle early.
runners_data.comment: Amerilis leads this line-up on our figures, rated 83, with a big speed figure of 80 in support. Her best placing, a 2nd, came two starts back, and she has both today's trip and ground covered — the raw ability here makes her the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Lumiere Des Etoile
runners_data.note: 61 days off the track and stepping down sharply from 7-8f to 5f — trainer has one winner from three runners in the past fortnight; genuine hold-up horse who needs more pace than All Hail is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Lumiere Des Etoile has managed nothing better than 4th in her last five and has yet to threaten the frame, her latest effort blank 61 days ago. She has raced over today's trip and rates 72, fifth of 10, though that lengthy absence leaves her fitness in question.

runners_data.name: Cashel Blue
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 5f on good last time out, making them the most in-form runner with the best course-and-distance profile in the field; prominent style aligns neatly with the projected race shape and W J Lee is a senior jockey booking.
runners_data.comment: Cashel Blue won last time out, 43 days ago, rounding off a progressive campaign that had also produced a 5th following two below-par efforts. She has raced over today's trip and rates 66, seventh of 10, though she'll need to defy that lengthy break to follow up.

runners_data.name: Boston Max
runners_data.note: Recent back-to-back wins are eye-catching form, but as a horse that naturally wants to race prominently, being shuffled to midfield by the race dynamic represents a style compromise; the form entitles them to be considered, yet the positional squeeze is a genuine concern at 5f.
runners_data.comment: Boston Max strung together back-to-back wins in the middle of his last five and continued that upward curve with a 2nd last time, 27 days ago. He has raced over today's trip and rates 66, sixth of 10 — a formful sort capable of another bold showing.

runners_data.name: Love Bomb
runners_data.note: Visor fitted and just 10 days since last run, but recent form over this trip on good ground reads 10th and 14th; a hold-up horse whose fade flag reinforces that the race shape is unlikely to suit, even with headgear intervention.
runners_data.comment: Love Bomb managed a fair 4th five starts back but has since found only rear-of-field or blank efforts, the latest just 10 days ago. She has raced over today's trip and rates 64, eighth of 10, leaving her hard to fancy on this recent evidence.

runners_data.name: Mini Cotai
runners_data.note: Tongue tie and hood fitted for a hold-up performer with modest form at this level — the redistribution to midfield reflects a race with too many rear-rankers for all to find their spot; ground form of 0W/0P at similar going adds to the concern.
runners_data.comment: Mini Cotai shaped better when 2nd three starts back but has faded since to a 9th and a blank effort, her latest just 10 days ago. She has raced over today's trip and rates 56, ninth of 10, though a decent speed figure of 70 offers a little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Another Nice'day
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field and carrying a fade flag; races hold-up by inclination but the mapping reflects the crowded hold-up division, and form figures of 006 in recent outings on good ground make a winning move hard to envisage.
runners_data.comment: Another Nice'day sits bottom of the field on our figures, rated 56, and was 6th last time, 17 days ago, in a mostly blank run of finishes. He has raced over today's trip, and a strong speed figure of 70 hints at hidden capability despite the poor form.

races.paceDynamic: All Hail is the lone confirmed front-runner and, crucially, is uncontested at the head of affairs — with no genuine pace rival looking to push past them from the gates, the tempo across this 5f on good-to-firm ground at Navan will be controlled and sustainable rather than frenetic. The Right One, Amerilis, and Cashel Blue are all prominent types who will look to sit close to the pace, creating a compact lead group, while Boston Max — a genuine front-runner by nature — has been mapped to midfield because the race already has more prominent horses than the map can absorb at the fore; of these Boston Max is the most likely to actually push up and challenge for a prominent pitch, with Amerilis the next most likely to secure one. The hold-up contingent (White Smoke, Lumiere Des Etoile, Mini Cotai, Another Nice'day) will be rearward in a race not truly set up to deliver the sustained gallop that would stretch the lead group and create gaps for closers to exploit. In a one-pacer scenario at a flat, tight 5f, the race shape strongly favours runners racing prominently or handy — particularly those with the tactical speed to attach to the lead group early and sustain it on quick ground — over hold-up operators who are genuinely out of their natural element here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If All Hail dictates a steady, uncontested tempo and the lead group rolls home in the straight without blowing up.
scenarios.body: All Hail sets a metronomic pace on good-to-firm and the prominent chasers — The Right One and Cashel Blue — have enough left to pounce in the final furlong where hold-up horses cannot close fast enough on a flat track.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Breaks Cover Early
scenarios.trigger: If Boston Max or Amerilis pushes hard from the gates and forces a genuinely contested early pace.
scenarios.body: The front group burns brighter than usual and the winner emerges from just off the pace as the leaders tire slightly inside the final furlong; The Right One, who handles this trip and going well, is ideally positioned to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Get Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is fractionally quicker than expected and the lead group flattens out in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: White Smoke or Lumiere Des Etoile, tracking midfield, could pick up the pieces if the leaders come back to the field — though both are genuinely hold-up types and this scenario relies on an unusually strong pace for a 5f handicap with one true front-runner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front-Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If All Hail is allowed to go so slowly that they simply stroll home unchallenged.
scenarios.body: An extreme version of Scenario A where the pace is so modest that All Hail's prominent rivals cannot summon sufficient finishing acceleration on quick ground to reel them in; fades in finish flags for All Hail make this the least probable outcome.

watchPoints.text: Cashel Blue is the in-form horse with the ideal course-and-distance profile — watch for them to track All Hail closely and quicken past them approaching the furlong pole.

Boston Max is a true prominent-style horse being squeezed out of their natural position by race shape — watch the opening furlong to see whether Chris Hayes pushes for the front or concedes midfield, as that decision will determine their chance entirely.

The Right One won last time over this exact trip but that victory came on soft ground — monitor market moves and paddock behaviour given the quicker surface today is the one genuine doubt about their participation at their best.

All Hail has a confirmed fade flag — if they look flat or under pressure passing the 2f pole despite leading unchallenged, the race will pivot sharply toward The Right One and Cashel Blue who are sitting just behind them.

The hold-up group (White Smoke, Lumiere Des Etoile, Mini Cotai, Another Nice'day) are collectively dependent on a stronger gallop than this race shape is likely to generate — if they are still well off the pace at halfway, discount them entirely.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Race

runners_data.name: Confused
runners_data.note: OR-120 three-year-old for Mrs Harrington who showed strong recent form (1/10f/Good) and has a solid 2/2 record on similar going; the lone front-runner here and likely to get an uncontested lead, though its style-fit score of 0.90 is a mild note that its performance level from a prominent rather than outright lead position may not fully translate.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out having previously finished fourth, but that pair of runs leaves him rated bottom of this five on both figures. He has form over today's distance, returns after 40 days, and carries 136lb from stall one.

runners_data.name: South Island
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien-trained three-year-old with a patchy recent record (best run a win over 9f on Soft) and 0W0P on similar going from five attempts; a natural prominent type who may find Confused's uncontested lead impossible to peg back from if unable to apply early pressure, and jockey Paddy Harnett (5lb claim) must find a clean passage.|
runners_data.comment: Rated the pick of this five, underlined by a 100 official mark and a strong speed figure to back it up. He has landed one of his last five starts and is proven over today's trip, making him the one to beat despite a 49-day absence.

runners_data.name: Summer Is Tomorrow
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's gelding carries a visor and is at the sharper end of fitness following a run just 13 days ago; in truth a front-running or prominent type, but with those slots already taken by Confused, it is likely to race in a position behind its comfort zone, and its style-fit tag of 0.92 suggests a meaningful discount applies to its chances if this shape does not open up.|
runners_data.comment: Summer Is Tomorrow was runner-up last time out. A ninth two starts back is the blot on his recent form, but he sits second of five on our figures backed by a strong speed number. Yet to score in his last five starts, he has form over today's distance and returns within a fortnight.

runners_data.name: Hard Promises
runners_data.note: Lightly raced at just one career start (third over 10f on Soft), so carries considerable unknown quantities, but an OR of 120 alongside Ben Coen in the saddle indicates significant stable confidence; the 69-day absence is a flag, but if fit and forward, a close-tracking role just off Confused could suit ideally.|
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced, with only one run to work from — a creditable third. He rates third of five on our figures, backed by a fair speed number, and has form over today's distance, though a 69-day absence adds a query.

runners_data.name: Mo Mhuirin
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's dual-role handler-jockey combination brings an OR-84 three-year-old who has placed twice over today's trip on Good ground; a naturally prominent-going type pushed to the back of this field by redistribution, meaning it will race further off the pace than it would choose — the style-fit score of 0.80 is the most significant discount in this field and limits its realistic winning chance.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and placed in each of her last three starts, having landed one three starts back. Rated fourth of five on our figures despite an 84 official mark, she has form over today's distance but needs more to trouble the principals.

races.paceDynamic: Confused is the lone confirmed front-runner in a five-horse field and should stride to the lead unchallenged from the off, setting what figures to be a measured, sustainable gallop over 1m2f on Good to Firm ground at Navan. South Island and Summer Is Tomorrow are both genuine prominent types, but with Confused already commanding the front, at least one of them will be unable to secure their natural position and will be pushed wider or slightly further back than ideal — Summer Is Tomorrow in particular is mapped to midfield precisely because the prominent berths are already occupied. Hard Promises is an unknown quantity stylistically, while Mo Mhuirin, a natural prominent racer, has been redistributed to the rear of the field by default, meaning this race is short of genuine hold-up horses and the tactical shape is front-to-back from the start. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or tracking profile — a horse able to sit just off Confused's uncontested lead and produce a clean, measured challenge in the straight without having to negotiate traffic will be best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Confused Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Confused bowls along at a comfortable, uncontested clip and the prominent trackers fail to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Confused dictates from flag to finish on Good to Firm ground that will reward a relaxed front-runner, and with no genuine pressing rival to quicken the pace, the leader's energy reserves remain intact into the final furlong. South Island or Hard Promises, tracking closely, are best positioned to challenge but must do so against a horse that has been untroubled throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Runs Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If a close-tracking rival, particularly Hard Promises or South Island, settles within a length of Confused and delivers a sustained challenge from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Confused's moderate gallop could leave enough petrol in the tank for a well-positioned tracker to hit the front smoothly without needing a dramatic finishing burst. Hard Promises, lightly raced and carrying class via a solid OR-120 mark, is the type who could benefit most from this controlled, quality-over-quantity scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runner Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and a horse switched wide and ridden late produces a strong closing run.
scenarios.body: Summer Is Tomorrow is a genuine prominent type mapped to midfield, so any late surge relies on a horse racing out of its natural role, making this the least structurally sound scenario. Mo Mhuirin, similarly redistributed to the rear, would also need everything to fall right — a slow tempo followed by a dramatic fade from those in front — which is unlikely given Confused's soundness on this going.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, No Clear Pacemaker
scenarios.trigger: If Confused misses the break or is unexpectedly challenged early, scrambling the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Without its only genuine front-runner dictating, the race becomes a messy contest where South Island and Summer Is Tomorrow compete for a contested lead, burning energy early on ground that punishes wasteful races. Hard Promises, with tactical flexibility and class on its side, could exploit the disarray, but this scenario requires multiple things going wrong simultaneously.

watchPoints.text: Confused's ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the pivotal factor — watch whether South Island or Summer Is Tomorrow attempts to press it into the first bend, which could fundamentally alter the energy cost for the leader.

Hard Promises is 69 days between runs with only one career start to its name — if it shows any signs of ring-rustiness or greenness early, its prominent tracking position could be wasted, but if it travels well it becomes a serious danger.

Summer Is Tomorrow's visor and competitive nature may lead it to race keenly from a position further back than ideal — jockey McMonagle will need to manage its energy carefully if it is to produce a meaningful challenge from midfield.

Mo Mhuirin's jockey and trainer being the same person (Andrew Slattery) is an unusual arrangement; note how early in the race it settles, as any tendency to race prominently against the grain of the mapped shape would confirm it cannot win from further back than its nature allows.

Going is reported as Good to Firm for this race despite the card header listing Good — confirm the official going stick reading before final assessment, as Good to Firm clearly favours the front-runner and a sustained gallop more than a slower Good surface would.

races.name: Navan Handicap

runners_data.name: Sonoran
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for G M Lyons who has shown ability at a mile-and-a-quarter on good ground (placed twice at the trip in similar conditions), but his recent form string includes plenty of mid-field finishes and he needs things to go right late; 11 days between runs is sharp and the stable's 14-day strike rate is modest at 1/20.|
runners_data.comment: Rated second of eleven on our figures, well clear of an 82 official mark, with two thirds among his last five starts. But he was well beaten last time out, and the stable have landed only one from 20 runners in a lean recent spell, a concern 11 days on.

runners_data.name: Beauparc
runners_data.note: Six-year-old veteran who has placed twice over today's course and distance and showed a clear affinity for 12f on good in his second placing; Nicola Burns claims 5lb which is significant, and 21 days since last run is acceptable — his hold-up style suits a race where late closers have a realistic chance if the pace holds.|
runners_data.comment: Rated third of eleven and above an 81 official mark, she was runner-up two starts back and has landed one of her last six starts. But her latest effort only reached sixth, and finding more will be needed 21 days on from stall eleven.

runners_data.name: Steel Cut
runners_data.note: Mapped as the confirmed front runner and is the race's key pace-setter, but his STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 flags that he is racing out of role relative to his recent runs; the small sample of good-ground form (1 run, no win or place) is a concern, and the five-pound claimer Sam Coen will need to judge the pace perfectly to keep him competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Found the frame two starts back in second but that form dipped either side, sandwiched by finishes of ninth and fifth. Rated 76, some way below an 80 official mark, he does have form over today's distance but ranks only eighth of eleven on our figures.

runners_data.name: Genoah
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins on standard and two course-and-distance placings at Navan to his name, making this track a genuine positive; the tongue-strap and hood combination has been present in his wins and his OR of 77 puts him near the top of this field — a forward position in this shape suits him well.|
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last five starts underline solid form, and he tops this field of eleven on our figures, well clear of a 77 official mark. A promising second last time out, and proven over today's distance and going, make him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Daonethatgotaway
runners_data.note: Front-foot operator who has won and placed multiple times over 12f on standard, but this is his first start in 99 days and his sole turf-going record offers a limited read; the 7lb claim from Joseph Harnett is an asset on paper but adds uncertainty, and his experience at the trip over stabling ground is not fully replicated today.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to justify a spot near the top on our figures, ranking ninth of eleven, and his latest effort ended unplaced. He does have a win among his last six starts and form over today's distance, but a 99-day absence leaves plenty to prove fitness-wise.

runners_data.name: Cala Bonita
runners_data.note: Four-year-old filly who won back-to-back times on standard over 10f and has since been tested on turf; her most recent turf run was a fourth over 12f on good which is directly relevant, and the tongue-strap has featured in both victories — Matthew J Smith has a 14-day strike rate of 1/12 suggesting the yard is ticking over.|
runners_data.comment: Two wins in her last five starts came three and four runs back, but the placings have since cooled to eighth and fourth. She ranks tenth of eleven on our figures, though she is proven over today's distance and going after a 40-day break.

runners_data.name: Lady Chartwell
runners_data.note: Her true running style is hold-up, but with more hold-up types than the map can place she is shifted to midfield on the chart — five consecutive finishing positions of 5th or worse including three double-figure results do not inspire confidence, and the 5lb claim from Patrick McGettigan does not compensate sufficiently for the weak form trajectory.|
runners_data.comment: Rated 81 on our figures, well clear of a 69 official mark despite three unplaced efforts in her last three starts, preceded by two fifth-place runs. Proven over today's distance and going, that gap hints at unlocked improvement, though still without a win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Letiza
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield mapping due to field congestion at the rear; 231 days off is a significant flag and her only win came on good ground over 10f, which is a positive match for today, but trainer Adrian Nicholls has a blank 14-day record and the lengthy absence makes this a speculative reappearance.|
runners_data.comment: A win among her last five starts came four runs back, but the placings either side have been modest, including an unplaced effort last time out. She rates fifth of eleven on our figures and is proven over today's distance, though a 231-day absence poses a big question.

runners_data.name: Raydamann
runners_data.note: Genuinely prominent in style but redistributed to midfield on the pace map — in reality, Chris Hayes is likely to push him forward to try and secure his natural position; his recent turf win came over an extended 18f on good which flags him as a stayer, and his last two starts over 10f on good were moderate, but the 12f trip here is shorter than his comfort zone.|
runners_data.comment: Well held in each of his last four starts, with only a sixth to show, and he remains without a win. Yet the clock tells a different story — a stand-out speed figure of 102 hints at latent ability, and he does have form over today's distance from stall two.

runners_data.name: Felix Somary
runners_data.note: Carries a notable "fades in finish" flag which is a serious concern in any scenario that requires a genuine late effort; his form is exclusively at shorter trips (6f-8f) and this step up to 1m2f on turf looks a significant ask — the 3-year-old allowance helps on weight but the form profile does not map onto today's requirements.|
runners_data.comment: His best effort, a fourth, came furthest back in his last five starts, with two ninths and two unplaced efforts since. He's seventh of eleven on our figures, though a fair speed figure and a return inside six weeks keep him in the shake-up.

runners_data.name: Admiral Will Brown
runners_data.note: Three-year-old whose four runs have all ended in finishes of 7th or worse, making him the lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 64; his true style is hold-up but is shown in midfield due to field redistribution, and Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim cannot offset a consistent record of trailing the field on good and soft ground alike.|
runners_data.comment: Rated bottom of this field of eleven, with a run of three sevenths and one eighth in his last four starts showing little spark. He does have form over today's distance, carrying 119lb from stall seven, but remains without a win and hard to fancy on these figures.

races.paceDynamic: Steel Cut is the confirmed front runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in an 11-runner field over 1m2f on good-to-firm ground at Navan, the early tempo figures to be controlled and sustainable rather than suicidal. Genoah, Daonethatgotaway, and Cala Bonita are all genuine prominent types who will press for position just off the lead, creating a small cluster at the head of affairs without materially burning out the pace. The field holds more prominent and hold-up horses than the map can accommodate cleanly — Raydamann, Letiza, Lady Chartwell, and Admiral Will Brown are all pushed out of their natural rear positions, with Raydamann the most likely to press forward and actually secure a spot near the pace given his redistribution profile. A single, uncontested front runner dictating a measured gallop on fast ground over a flat mile-and-a-quarter strongly favours horses who can sit just off the leader, travel kindly in a prominent position, and produce a sustained finish — the prominent-to-midfield tracking profile is the chief beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steel Cut Dictates Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Steel Cut is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable gallop with no challenger willing to close him down before the home turn.
scenarios.body: Steel Cut sets a steady, controlled tempo and the field settles into a rhythm behind him, with Genoah, Daonethatgotaway, and Cala Bonita tracking in a tight group just off the pace; when the tempo lifts in the straight, the horse who has travelled best just behind the leader collects the prize. Prominent racers who have saved energy through the middle portion of the race are ideally placed and the fast ground rewards their forward position without punishing them for using up early fuel.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Injected Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If Raydamann or another redistributed prominent type surges to challenge Steel Cut after the halfway point, lifting the overall tempo.
scenarios.body: The increased pace quickens the race up earlier than expected, burning off horses who are positioned too far back and stretching the field entering the straight; horses with genuine stamina at the trip who have been settled in midfield now pick off the weakened leaders. This scenario opens the door to the better-staying hold-up types who have the class to close on a genuinely run race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and the field strings out in the straight, allowing true hold-up types to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Steel Cut's controlled early gallop paradoxically creates a congested, slowly-run affair until the final two furlongs, at which point the hold-up horses who have conserved energy make their runs simultaneously. However, this scenario is tempered by the fact that several nominally hold-up runners here — Letiza, Lady Chartwell, Admiral Will Brown — are redistributed from their natural positions and may not achieve the clean late run their profile requires.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively strong on fast ground and the hold-up horses simply cannot close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Steel Cut's lead proves unassailable as the good-to-firm ground keeps the pace honest throughout, and the horses pressing from behind find they have used too much energy to sustain their challenge; the winner is the horse on the front end or closest to it throughout. This shape is least likely given Steel Cut's limited recent form and the OR compression in this handicap.

watchPoints.text: Steel Cut's early pace judgement is critical — if Sam Coen (5lb claimer) misjudges the gallop and either goes too fast or allows a challenger to push him wide on the bend, the entire race shape collapses and the prominent runners behind him are denied a true test.

Raydamann is redistributed from his natural prominent position — watch whether Chris Hayes sends him forward before the race settles, because if he does succeed in getting to the pace, it injects a second genuine front-runner into the equation and the race becomes materially faster than the single-pacer scenario assumes.

Genoah's course-and-distance form is a strong positive, but his last five runs on good turf produced seven wins from fifteen tries at the sim-going level — if his form is patchy on this surface, his prominent position may cost him late in the straight.

Felix Somary's "fades in finish" flag combined with a step up from 6f-8f to 1m2f is a significant safety and competitive concern — connections and punters should note this horse may drop out tamely and become an obstacle in the straight for runners coming from behind.

The going report consistently logs Good To Firm for all three 1m2f races at Navan today — conditions are uniform and faster than the declared Good, meaning horses whose best form is on softer ground (Sonoran's soft placing, Letiza's standard form) face a hidden going question that their sim-going records only partially answer.

races.name: Navan Racing Festival 14th & 15th November Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Rising Sky
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner carrying 142lbs; goes on good ground and won last time over 10f at Sandown, but steps up to 12f here and faces the class test of controlling from the front in a 14-runner handicap — style-fit tag reflects it may not get the prominent berth as cleanly as expected with traffic around.
runners_data.comment: Rising Sky won one of her last six starts, with a third-place effort too, and returns just eight days after a blank latest run. She races from stall 2, sits fourth of 14 on our figures, but the inconsistent finishes elsewhere are the risk.

runners_data.name: Arch Enemy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type resuming after 105 days off, a lengthy break that raises fitness questions; has a worrying tendency to fade late, has not shown good-to-firm form in recent history, and the headgear absence makes it hard to find an angle.
runners_data.comment: Arch Enemy is proven over today's trip and ground and ranks second of 14 on our figures, backed by a smart speed figure of 74. She's without a win in her last five starts, and a 105-day layoff is the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Deuteronomy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 10f at Leopardstown on heavy and recorded a flat course win; 23 days since last run is ideal, wears a hood, and is one of the few horses here whose natural style genuinely suits the expected race shape — strong contender for the prominent berth behind Rising Sky.
runners_data.comment: Deuteronomy scored a win among his last six starts but has also finished as low as eighth twice, a mixed record. Fit again 23 days on, he has form over today's trip and ground and rates eighth of 14 - solidly midfield rather than a threat.

runners_data.name: Jazz Forever
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has shown some ability over 13f but is a hold-up type with a pattern of late fading; a short break of eight days is fine but the big-field prominent bias works against him, and his best recent efforts have come at staying trips longer than today's 1m2f.
runners_data.comment: Jazz Forever is yet to win in his last five starts, though a third-place effort shows some ability, and he's fresh from just eight days ago. He has form over today's trip and rates seventh of 14, with inconsistent finishes either side of that placed run.

runners_data.name: Robot Rock
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by A J Martin, back eight days after a flat effort; best form came when finishing second over 12f on standard in heavy conditions, making the good-to-firm ground a genuine concern — just four of six similar-going runs have produced any hint of form.
runners_data.comment: Robot Rock is winless in his last five starts, his one runner-up effort now the oldest of them and his latest run a blank just eight days ago. He has form over today's trip and sits tenth of 14 on our figures, with modest efforts elsewhere in that sequence.

runners_data.name: Autocrat
runners_data.note: True hold-up type whose natural position is at the rear; the redistribution to midfield on the map reflects a field congested with closers — it won over 10f on standard ground and the step to a flat 12f on fast ground is an open question, with a 57-day break adding further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Autocrat tops our ratings on 75, with a fourth and a follow-up win among his last five starts backing that figure, plus a strong speed figure of 69. The 57-day break since his last run is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Trishuli River
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing a tongue-tie and cheekpieces who has placed twice at 10f-12f range on standard ground; eight days since last run and a draw in a competitive 14-runner handicap are neutral factors, but its recent run of zeros from prominent positions in similar company is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Trishuli River is yet to win in her last five starts but has been placed twice, fresh just eight days on. She has form over today's trip and ground, ranks third of 14 on our figures, though her latest two starts have dipped below that level.

runners_data.name: Cleopatra's Needle
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old wearing a hood, trained by H Rogers and ridden by the experienced Chris Hayes; has placed five times in recent outings including two wins, goes on good ground (11 from 15 similar-going runs showed place form), and the prominent style over 1m2f on this surface is a very strong fit.
runners_data.comment: Cleopatra's Needle is yet to win in her last five starts despite three runner-up efforts, and is back 21 days on. She has form over today's trip and ground, rates sixth of 14, with a useful speed figure of 74 - converting those places remains the task.

runners_data.name: Thegooseiscooked
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent racer with a win and four places from nine good-to-firm runs in its history; recent form reads poorly with back-to-back zeros at 10f and 8f, and today's 12f trip over a true flat track may ask a different question — worth monitoring in the market.
runners_data.comment: Thegooseiscooked is yet to win in her last five starts, though a fourth-place effort is the highlight, and she's back 36 days on. She has form over today's trip and ground, rates fifth of 14, with a strong speed figure of 73 - the layoff is the query.

runners_data.name: Retro Gal
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from the Henry de Bromhead yard, a hold-up type that carries just 129lbs; has run seven times in eight going-similar races without winning and posted a string of seventh-place finishes, but the yard's 14-day strike rate of 1/15 and the youth angle make this one worth watching if the pace scenario turns chaotic.
runners_data.comment: Retro Gal has been well held in each of her last five starts, without a win and often no better than seventh, leaving little to work with on figures. She is fresh just 10 days on, ranking 11th of 14, and looks up against it on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Copper Craft
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up horse at heart, held up in all recent starts; the map shows it in midfield because the field is overloaded with closers, and its actual racing position will likely be further back — wears a hood, placed twice at 10f-12f on standard and soft, but needs more pace than Rising Sky is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Copper Craft was placed second, third and fourth in three of his last five starts, but his latest two efforts have been far weaker, clouding the picture. He has form over today's trip, rates 12th of 14 on our figures, and needs to rediscover that earlier level.

runners_data.name: One For Teigan
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse from P Sweeney's yard, a trainer with a modest 14-day record of 0/2; its natural style is to race from the back but a congested field of closers means it will struggle to find clear air late — recent form of five zeros offers little encouragement regardless of shape.
runners_data.comment: One For Teigan has been comfortably held in each of her last five starts, unplaced bar a ninth, with little there to encourage. She returns 30 days on and has form over today's trip, but ranks 13th of 14 on our figures with plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Haughty
runners_data.note: Another genuine closer that the map cannot accommodate at the rear; won over 10f on good in the past (1W1P from nine good-going runs), but 69 days off and the natural racing position being compromised by a field stacked with hold-up types are real obstacles — Killian Leonard keeps the faith but improvement is needed.
runners_data.comment: Haughty has yet to win in her last five starts and was no better than sixth in that run, though our figures rate her above her official mark, helped by a solid speed figure of 64. A 69-day absence is the concern, and she rates ninth of 14.

runners_data.name: Gold Dublooms
runners_data.note: A fader at the finish on the evidence of its form flag, with the redistribution reflecting that it, too, is a true hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield slot; wears a tongue-tie, is 40 days since last run, and has five consecutive mid-to-rear finishes — needs a strong pace that this race shape simply may not provide.
runners_data.comment: Gold Dublooms ranks last of 14 on our figures, with his best form a third-place effort followed only by much weaker showings. He has form over today's trip and returns 40 days on, but there's little in that sequence to inspire confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Rising Sky is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is expected to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested tempo on good-to-firm ground over 1m2f at Navan. Deuteronomy and Trishuli River are the likeliest horses to press from a prominent position, but neither has the profile to force Rising Sky into a lung-busting early gallop, meaning the pace should be honest rather than scorching. The redistribution note is critical: Autocrat, One For Teigan, Copper Craft, Haughty and Gold Dublooms are all true hold-up types pushed into midfield slots on the map because this field simply has too many closers to fit naturally at the rear — in reality, several will be further back than their mapped position suggests, which compresses the field behind a single leader and reduces the likelihood of a truly strong finishing kick from deep. This race shape — a moderate, uncontested lead — most favours genuine prominent racers who can track the steady gallop of Rising Sky and pounce at the two-pole, rather than deep closers who need a strong pace to generate their run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Lead, Track And Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Rising Sky bowls along at a comfortable uncontested tempo and the race is decided by who tracks closest into the straight.
scenarios.body: Rising Sky controls from the front with Deuteronomy and Cleopatra's Needle sitting closest in a patient chase; the 1m2f trip on good-to-firm suits those with a high cruising speed rather than a late burst, and the winner emerges from the prominent group in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Rising Sky goes too fast for this class of race and Deuteronomy or Trishuli River surge through to dominate the finish.
scenarios.body: A moderate handicap leader setting what feels like a comfortable clip can still find the pace excessive for a 0-60 field on quick ground, gifting the race to the prominent pair who have conserved energy in second and third.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Eyecatcher Delivers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and one of the redistributed hold-up types produces a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Copper Craft or Autocrat, though pushed wider in the field than their natural position, could capitalise if the front two over-cook it on fast ground; their style-fit discount means this needs both a quicker gallop and a clean passage, making it the third-most likely shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Rising Sky ties up dramatically and the entire field bunches entering the straight, turning the finish into a scramble.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up types unable to get to the rear, mid-race crowding could cause trouble in running, leaving a chaotic final furlong where a fresh horse like Retro Gal or one carrying low weight benefits from a clear run.

watchPoints.text: Rising Sky (Patrick McGettigan 5lb claim) sets the entire race shape — if it is allowed a soft lead from flag to finish at this class level, horses tracking it like Cleopatra's Needle and Deuteronomy become significantly more dangerous than their ratings suggest.

Monitor Autocrat, Copper Craft and One For Teigan in the paddock and early race; all three are true hold-up types redistributed on the map, and if they break forward unexpectedly they could force an uncharacteristic pace increase that alters the race shape entirely.

Cleopatra's Needle's recent run of four consecutive places (two wins in last five) on good ground, ridden by Chris Hayes, makes it the most tactically dangerous prominent type — if it gets a clean slot just off the early leader it could prove hard to peg back in the final furlong.

Deuteronomy's headgear (hood) and 23-day freshness angle are worth noting — R P Burns has a quiet yard record (0/4 in 14 days) but this horse has two wins from nine prominent efforts on similar ground, and its style is perfectly aligned with the expected race shape.

Retro Gal (Henry de Bromhead, 3yo, 129lbs) is the least exposed runner in the field — while form is unimpressive, the combination of light weight, top yard and a chaotic finish scenario (Scenario D) would bring this filly into the frame as a place dark horse.
